catalysts.headline: Shares partially recovered (+6.9% reported) the day after the Sept 29 selloff — this is a bounce, NOT the underlying catalyst.
Shares partly recovered, +6.9% to $26.21, as some analysts argued the prior day's selloff was overdone relative to price targets

AMT-130 (Huntington's disease gene therapy) 48-month Phase I/II data update: Unified Huntington's Disease Rating Scale (UHDRS) showed 44% slowing of disease progression vs. updated external control — NOT statistically significant (p=0.144), down from a previously reported 75% slowing at 36 months. Shares fell ~37% (from ~$39.11 to ~$24.40). Company argued the 48-month readout understates the true effect due to missing data and dropout bias among faster-progressing external-control patients, and said 36-month data from 15 high-dose patients remains robust and underpins the planned BLA filing.

uniQure discloses additional 48-month AMT-130 Huntington's disease data: 80% slowing of disease progression (cUHDRS) at 36 months, but only 44% at 48 months (not statistically significant durability), alongside continued BLA priority-review process (submitted 2026-09-02)
catalysts.impact: Shares fell ~37% intraday/close from ~$39.11 to ~$24.51 on the session; subsequent shareholder securities-litigation investigation notices followed

catalysts.headline: uniQure submits Biologics License Application (BLA) to FDA for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease, requesting priority review; potential approval as soon as Q2 2027 if granted
catalysts.impact: Sets up the September data readout as a key event

catalysts.headline: Q2 2026 results: revenue $5.8M (vs. $5.3M Q2 2025), net loss $81.1M (-$1.22/share, GAAP); cash & investments $810.3M as of 2026-06-30 following a $259M follow-on offering completed in June 2026.

notes: IMPORTANT for dashboard: the real catalyst behind QURE's September move was the Sept 29, 2026 AMT-130 48-month Huntington's disease data update (44% slowing of progression, NOT statistically significant, p=0.144) — a ~37% single-day drop. The Sept 30 '+6.9% partial recovery' noted in the prior snapshot is just the bounce off that drop, not an independent catalyst. Separately (outside the ~6-month catalyst window, so not listed above but relevant background): shares fell >35% on 2026-03-02 after the FDA said existing AMT-130 data were insufficient for a marketing application, and the stock later rallied in mid-June 2026 when the company announced plans to proceed with a BLA filing after further FDA feedback (exact June date not confirmed, so omitted from the dated catalyst list). Theme 'Biotech Catalyst' fits well given the binary regulatory/clinical-readout dependency. FY2024/FY2025 annual EPS not established this session (WebSearch budget exhausted).
